canonical.name: Prior-predictive joint law from a prior and parameter-measurable sampling kernel
canonical.reason: The inspected published supplier constructs the product joint probability and prior-predictive marginal, with its complete kernel-integration proof.

A standard-Borel data coordinate factors the posterior RCD into a data-indexed kernel unique marginal-almost-everywhere

sources.title: Andrew Gelman, John B. Carlin, Hal S. Stern, David B. Dunson, Aki Vehtari, and Donald B. Rubin, Bayesian Data Analysis, Third Edition
sources.locator: Chapter 1 §§1.1–1.3, printed pp. 3–8 (PDF pp. 13–18); complete six-page text extract inspected.

contents.name: §1.1 The three steps of Bayesian data analysis
contents.reason: This broad applied workflow includes model-fit assessment and computation; BCS-01 supplies model and conditioning foundations rather than the entire analysis workflow.

contents.name: §1.2 Parameters, data, and predictions notation
contents.reason: These are conventional applied symbols rather than a result needed for the measurable-space model and posterior-kernel definitions authored here.

contents.name: §1.2 Observational units and variables
contents.reason: This applied data-record discussion imposes no general kernel or posterior theorem and is outside the foundational probability scope of this pair.

contents.name: §1.2 Exchangeability
contents.reason: The current plan treats exchangeability as a modeling assumption alongside hierarchical models and explicitly avoids a finite de Finetti conclusion.

contents.name: §1.2 Explanatory variables
contents.reason: Covariate handling is model-specific and does not alter the prior-kernel or conditional-law definitions in this foundational pair.

contents.name: §1.2 Hierarchical modeling
contents.reason: The current plan assigns hierarchical probability kernels, hyperpriors, and partial pooling to the later BCS-05 pair.

contents.name: §1.3 Bayesian inference as conditioning on observed data
contents.reason: The A-page definition gives the measure-theoretic conditional-law meaning and separates an RCD from a data-indexed version.

contents.name: §1.3 Probability notation for densities and mass functions
contents.reason: The source suppresses reference measures in its density notation; this pair states kernel and measurable-space data explicitly instead.

contents.name: §1.3 Bayes rule for posterior densities
contents.reason: The general density quotient needs joint measurability and valid finite-positive evidence hypotheses, which the current plan assigns to BCS-02.

contents.name: §1.3 Prior-predictive distribution by integrating the joint model
contents.reason: The published kernel-integration lemma proves the joint-law and prior-predictive marginal identities for arbitrary measurable spaces.

contents.name: §1.3 Posterior predictive distribution
contents.reason: Future-outcome prediction is assigned to BCS-04 and is not part of the present posterior-existence claims.

contents.name: §1.3 Likelihood as a function of the parameter at fixed data
contents.reason: The published likelihood-density definition supplies this term and explicitly adds no parameter measurability or joint measurability.

contents.name: §1.3 Posterior odds and likelihood ratios
contents.reason: Posterior odds and model-evidence comparisons belong to the planned BCS-06 pair, with proper-prior evidence conditions.

sources.title: Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules! An Introduction to Applied Bayesian Modeling
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1.1–2.1.4 and §§2.3.1–2.3.6; complete selected sections of the official HTML chapter inspected.

contents.name: §2.1.1 Prior probability model
contents.reason: The A-page definition states a proper prior probability on the measurable parameter space.

contents.name: §2.1.2 Conditional probability and likelihood
contents.reason: The A-page definition represents the experiment by a parameter-measurable sampling probability kernel.

contents.name: Conditional versus unconditional event probability
contents.reason: The A-page definition uses conditional-law identities and explicitly does not define a posterior by dividing by a zero-probability event.

contents.name: §2.1.3 Normalizing constant in the finite event model
contents.reason: The example computes each finite prior-predictive mass and verifies the normalized posterior on every positive-mass data value.

contents.name: §2.1.4 Posterior probability model via Bayes rule
contents.reason: The local finite calculation verifies both posterior probabilities and separately leaves the impossible-data version arbitrary.

contents.name: §2.3.1 Prior probability model for a random parameter
contents.reason: The A-page definition supplies the prior probability on the measurable parameter space used to mix sampling laws.

contents.name: §2.3.2 Binomial data model
contents.reason: The present pair defines general sampling kernels; the planned conjugate-family pair handles the Binomial update examples.

contents.name: §2.3.3 Binomial likelihood function
contents.reason: The Binomial likelihood-specific update is assigned to BCS-03 and is not needed for the general posterior-kernel interface.

contents.name: §2.3.4 Finite normalizing constant for the countable-parameter example
contents.reason: The example forms the prior-predictive masses and verifies normalization by summing the two geometric sampling laws.

contents.name: §2.3.5 Posterior probability model for the random parameter
contents.reason: The finite example gives the complete data-indexed posterior and checks its conditional rectangle identities.

contents.name: §2.3.6 Posterior shortcut and proportionality
contents.reason: The broad prior-times-likelihood formula requires explicit density and evidence hypotheses, which BCS-02 treats separately.
